selectedResourceCatalog.name: recon
selectedResourceCatalog.description: Investigate a question through code, documents, history, or other available evidence when discoveries can change your explanation and the question you need to answer.

selectedResourceCatalog.name: diagnostic-questioning
selectedResourceCatalog.description: Use when a conversation can resolve uncertainty about another person's intent, priorities, or experience. Let each answer revise your understanding and guide the next question.

selectedResourceCatalog.name: interpretive-synthesis
selectedResourceCatalog.description: Use when new details change your understanding of a situation, and that revised understanding changes what earlier observations mean or which question is worth pursuing.

selectedResourceCatalog.name: observational-grounding
selectedResourceCatalog.description: Use when observations seem to disagree, or a conclusion depends on an uncertain relationship between what was observed and what it is taken to show. Relate the evidence to its source and conditions as you investigate.

selectedResourceCatalog.name: relational-continuity
selectedResourceCatalog.description: Use when wording needs to carry the work forward in conversation, a summary, or a handoff. Preserve the concerns and relationships that make the next contribution meaningful.
